texts.preamble: Food Inspector/Food Safety Officer vs Sh Akash Aggarwal on 29 February, 2016 In The Court Of Shri Amar Nath: District & Sessions Judge New Delhi Crl. Appeal No. 96/12 Food Inspector/Food Safety Officer, Department of Pfa Govt. of Nct of Delhi, A20 Lawrence Road Indl. Area,New Delhi110035. ....Ap versus Sh Akash Aggarwal S/o Sh. Madan Gopal M/s Chanchal Kiryana Store Shop No.162, Gali Masjid Tevar Khan, Naya Bans Delhi110006. R/o 1698, Pratap Estate Chunna Mandi, Pahar Ganj Delhi110056. ....Re Date of Institution of Appeal : 12.12.2012. Judgment reserved on : 22.02.2016. Judgment announced on : 29.02.2016. J U D G M E N T
texts.facts: Notice of the appeal was given to the respondent who has resisted the same submitting that the appeal is not within limitation. The allegations of the complainant in brief are that on 15.09.2010 at about 1:30PM Sh. A. K. Singh, Food Inspector purchased a sample of Lal Mirch Powder, an article of food for analysis from Sh.Akash Aggarwal(respondent herein) where the said food article was found stored for sale of human consumption and where Sh. Akash Aggarwal was found vending the article of food at the time of taking the sample. The sample was taken under the supervision of Sh. R. K. Sharma, SDM/LHA. The sample consisted of 3x500 grams of Lal Mirch Powder taken as such in original sealed condition in poly packets having no label declaration and without vegetarian symbol for sale to the customer. Sample was divided into three equal parts then and there by putting one sealed packet as one counter part of sample. Each counter part containing the sample was Food Inspector vs. Akash Aggarwal separately packed, fastened and sealed according to the PFA Act, 1954 & Rules,1955. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and wrapper of the sample counter parts containing the sample. Notice in Form VI was given to Sh. Akash Aggarwal and the price of sample of Rs.150/ was also paid to him vide vendor receipt dated 15.09.2010. Panchnama too was prepared at the spot. All the documents prepared by the Food Inspector were signed by Sh. Akash Aggarwal and by other witness Sh. J. S Bisht, FA. One counterpart of the sample bearing LHA Code Number 42/LHA/29503 in intact condition alongwith copy of memo in Form VII in sealed packet and another copy of memo in Form VII under sealed cover were sent separately to the Public Analyst, Delhi on 16.09.2010 and remaining two counterparts of the sample alongwith the two copies of memos in Form VII in sealed packet were deposited with the SDM/LHA in intact conditions on 16.09.2010. All copies of Memos in Form VII bear the seal impression with which sample counterparts were sealed. Public Analyst analyzed the sample and found the sample is misbranded. The Public Analyst vide his report number PFA/Enf./2389/2010 dated 04.10.2010 has reported that the sample is misbranded because there is complete violation of rule 32 and Rule 42(zzz)(17) of PFA Rules,1955, however, chillies power conform Food Inspector vs. Akash Aggarwal to standard. The Public Analyst has also reported in his report regarding label :Without any label and without vegetarian symbol. As such, the respondent has violated the provisions of Section 7 of the PFA Act, 1954 r/w section 2(ix) (k) of PFA Act, 1954 and also violated the provisions of Rule 32 & Rule 42(zzz)(17) of PFA Rules, 1955 which is punishable u/s 16(1)(a) of PFA Act,1954. 4. A notice was framed against the respondent by the then Ld. ACMM2, New Delhi vide order dated 16.07.2011 and the matter was fixed up for the evidence of the complainant. Appellant was sentenced to SI for the period of one day i.e till the rising of the court and to pay a fine of Rs.15,000/ and in default of payment of fine, SI for 15 days vide order dated 08.10.2012. 5. Feeling aggrieved , the appellant has challenged the impugned order on account of inadequate sentence awarded by the court of the then Ld.ACMM2, New Delhi on the following grounds: I.

Under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (5 of 1898) (a) from a sentence of death passed by a court of Sessions or by a High Court in the exercise of its original criminal Thirty days The date of jurisdiction. sentence (b)from any other sentence or any order not being an order of acquittal Food Inspector vs. Akash Aggarwal to the High Court Sixty days. Counsel for the appellant has contended that the State has sought condonation of delay in filing the appeal against the inadequate sentence awarded by the court of the then Ld.ACMM02, New Delhi on the ground that approval to file the appeal was received in prosecution branch on 29.11.2012 and the period prior to that was consumed by the normal processes of office procedure in obtaining the permission to appeal. 10. He further contended that there is no specific time limitation for filing the appeal in Sessions Court under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. The limitation shall be six months where the appeal is preferred by the public servant before the Hon'ble High Court and as such, in the amended CrPC the time limitation in filing the appeal in the Sessions court may also be six months. If it is not so, then the reason for occurring of the delay has been well Food Inspector vs. Akash Aggarwal explained in the paragraph 2 of the application. 11. Per contra Ld. Counsel for the respondent has refuted the aforesaid line of arguments whilst making the submissions that there is a delay in preferring the present appeal and thus, it cannot be entertained, therefore, the same is liable to be dismissed on this ground alone. It is further argued that this appeal would be governed by Article 115 (b) of the Limitation Act, 1963 which prescribes 30 days period of limitation from the date of order against the inappropriate sentence awarded by the Food Inspector/Food Safety Officer vs Sh Akash Aggarwal on 29 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83788022/ 3 court. 12. The expression 'sufficient cause' in Section 5 of the Limitation Act, should receive a liberal construction so as to advance substantial justice when the delay is not on account of any dilatory practice, want of bonafides, deliberate in action of negligence on the part of the appellant. His Lordship went to state further that the law regarding the condonation of delay has got substantially changed from the stage of the judgment of Ram Lal, Chhote Lal & Moti Lal vs. Rewa Coal Field Pvt. Ltd., AIR 1962 SC 361 where the Hon'ble Apex Court was of the opinion that each day's delay has to be explained but this law has been toned down substantially to the extent that now the quantum of delay has not been considered to be material. Even in the latest judgment of the Apex Court, as reported in Executive Officer, Antiyur Town Panchayat Vs. G. Arumugam, (2015) 3 Supreme Court Cases 569, their Lordships [LEAKAGE_MASK] the impugned order after condoning the delay of 1373 days in filing the second appeal. Food Inspector vs. Akash Aggarwal 15. In AIR 1996 Supreme Court 2750, Special Tehsildar, Land Acquisiton, Kerala versus K.V. Ayisumma, it has been held by the Apex Court which is reproduced as under : "It is now settled law that when the delay was occasioned at the behest of the Government, it would be very difficult to explain the day to day delay. 20. Ld. Court of the then ACMM02, New Delhi recorded the guilt of the accused on 08.10.2012 where in lenient view was sought on account of misbranded sample as per the report of Public Analyst.
